title: Complexe de De Rham à puissance divisée [conférence de 1976 à l’IHÉS] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This page is not from the 1976 notes on the divided-power de Rham complex. It is a stray typescript page, numbered '- 45 - IX' with archive pagination 363, from Grothendieck's SGA 7 I, Exposé IX ('Modèles de Néron et monodromie'), §§4.4–4.5. Both neighbouring pages are handwritten notes on divided-power algebras, so the page is misfiled.

First paragraph (end of the proof of 4.4). Setting: an abelian variety A_K over the fraction field K of a henselian DVR with finite residue field F_q. The Tate module T_ℓ carries the filtration from the Néron model: fixed part, toric part, and the dual (character-type) quotient. Earlier on the page the Frobenius eigenvalues on the toric piece and on the last piece were stated as (q^n ε_i) and (ε_i), with ε_i roots of unity.
- The orthogonality and duality formula (4.1.2) pairs the toric part of A with the last piece of the dual A'. Via the pairing T_ℓ(A) × T_ℓ(A') → Z_ℓ(1), with Frobenius acting by q^n on the target, it gives eigenvalues q^n/(q^n ε_i) = ε_i^{-1} on the last piece.
- Since each ε_i is a root of unity, ε_i^{-1} equals its complex conjugate.
- The multiset {ε_i} is the set of roots of a polynomial with integer coefficients, so it is stable under complex conjugation.
- Hence {ε_i^{-1}} = {ε_i}, which is the last assertion of 4.4.

Section 4.5 (start of the application of 4.3 a) to the local conductor of abelian schemes). Assume k algebraically closed; the footnote says k perfect suffices, by passing to the strict henselisation. Recall the definition from SGA 5 X 6.2 / Raynaud's Bourbaki talk:
- For a finite étale commutative ℓ-group F_K (ℓ ≠ p), choose a finite Galois extension K'/K with group Γ splitting F_K, so F_K corresponds to a finite Γ-module M.
- Let Sw = Sw(K'/K, Z_ℓ) be the projective Z_ℓ[Γ]-module realising the Swan character.
- Set α_s(F_K) = length Hom_{Z_ℓ[Γ]}(Sw, M).
- This is independent of K'.

The page breaks off where projectivity of Sw is about to be used: it makes α_s additive in exact sequences. The continuation in SGA 7 IX uses 4.3 a) to show that the Swan conductor of T_ℓ(A) is independent of ℓ and is the 'wild part' of the conductor of A.
errors: No mathematical error. The stability of {ε_i} under conjugation relies on the characteristic polynomial having integer coefficients, which was established earlier in 4.4 and is used here without comment.
Typographical: 'derniere' lacks its accent; 'Hom_{Z_ℓ(Γ)}' should read Z_ℓ[Γ].
Archival: the page belongs to the SGA 7 IX typescript, not to the divided-power de Rham notes of cote 136 (misfiled leaf).

ideas.what: Frobenius eigenvalues on the toric piece and on the last piece of the monodromy filtration of T_ℓ of an abelian variety with semistable-type reduction are q^n·(roots of unity) and roots of unity; the second set is closed under inversion, deduced via the duality pairing (4.1.2)
ideas.modern_name: Weights of Frobenius on the graded pieces of the Néron/monodromy filtration (weight-monodromy for abelian varieties)

ideas.what: Swan conductor of a finite étale ℓ-group defined as the length of Hom_{Z_ℓ[Γ]}(Sw_{K'/K}, M), using the projective Swan module
ideas.modern_name: Swan conductor via the Swan representation (Serre's projective Z_ℓ[Γ]-module)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Serre (Swan module projectivity), Grothendieck–Raynaud (SGA 5 X; Raynaud, Sém. Bourbaki 286)
ideas.where_published: SGA 5 Exp. X §6; SGA 7 I Exp. IX §4.5

ideas.what: Application to the local conductor of abelian schemes (ℓ-independence of the Swan conductor of T_ℓ(A))
ideas.modern_name: Conductor of an abelian variety, wild part / Swan conductor

deep.surprise_reason: This is a typescript page of the published SGA 7 Exposé IX, misfiled among the 1976 divided-power notes; its content is in print. The only point of interest is archival: a stray SGA 7 leaf sits in cote 136.
transcription_corrections: 'Hom_{Z_ℓ(Γ)}(Sw,M)' should be 'Hom_{Z_ℓ[Γ]}(Sw,M)'; the typescript uses round brackets but square brackets are meant.
'la derniere assertion' is 'la dernière assertion' in the typescript, with the accent slightly misprinted.
Page header '- 45 - IX' and archive number 363 identify the page as SGA 7 Exp. IX; the handwritten '166' at bottom left is the archive folio number.
